I've attached NO2 (Q1 2023 average) data for 33 London boroughs and a list showing which boroughs are geographic neighbors of each other.

Question: You can use a statistical method such as Getis-Ord Gi*, or any other method you choose, to identify boroughs where there is an unusually intense CONCENTRATION of high NO2 (Q1 2023 average) (a HOT spot) or low NO2 (Q1 2023 average) (a COLD spot), considering each borough TOGETHER WITH its neighbors as one combined local area.

This is different from asking whether a borough simply resembles its immediate neighbors -- instead, you are testing whether the COMBINED total (the borough together with its neighbors) is unusually large or small compared to the citywide average, regardless of how similar the borough is to any one neighbor individually.

Note: a borough whose own value is missing should not itself be reported as a hot or cold spot in your final answer. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement your chosen method directly using only pandas and numpy. If your method produces a z-score, use the standard critical values: |z| > 1.96 for 95% confidence, |z| > 2.576 for 99% confidence.

End your response with exactly one line listing every borough you identified, using HOT for hot spot and COLD for cold spot, and including the computed real number (e.g. a z-score) for each:

import pandas as pd

# Load the datasets again
no2_data = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_no2_Q1_2023.csv')
adjacency_data = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Merge the adjacency data with NO2 data to get the NO2 values for neighbors
merged_data = adjacency_data.merge(no2_data, on='borough', how='left', suffixes=('', '_borough'))
merged_data = merged_data.merge(no2_data, left_on='neighbor', right_on='borough', how='left', suffixes=('', '_neighbor'))

# Calculate combined NO2 values
combined_no2 = merged_data.groupby('borough').agg(
    combined_no2_value=('avg_no2_value', lambda x: x.sum() if x.notnull().all() else None)
).reset_index()

# Include the borough's own NO2 value
combined_no2 = combined_no2.merge(no2_data, on='borough', how='left', suffixes=('', '_original'))
combined_no2['combined_no2_value'] = combined_no2['combined_no2_value'] + combined_no2['avg_no2_value']

# Filter out boroughs with missing values
combined_no2 = combined_no2[combined_no2['combined_no2_value'].notnull()]

print(combined_no2)
```

import pandas as pd

# Load the datasets again
no2_data = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_no2_Q1_2023.csv')
adjacency_data = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Merge the adjacency data with NO2 data to get the NO2 values for neighbors
merged_data = adjacency_data.merge(no2_data, on='borough', how='left', suffixes=('', '_borough'))
merged_data = merged_data.merge(no2_data, left_on='neighbor', right_on='borough', how='left', suffixes=('', '_neighbor'))

# Calculate combined NO2 values
combined_no2 = merged_data.groupby('borough').agg(
    combined_no2_value=('avg_no2_value', lambda x: x.sum() if x.notnull().all() else None)
).reset_index()

# Include the borough's own NO2 value
combined_no2 = combined_no2.merge(no2_data, on='borough', how='left', suffixes=('', '_original'))
combined_no2['combined_no2_value'] = combined_no2['combined_no2_value'] + combined_no2['avg_no2_value']

# Filter out boroughs with missing values
combined_no2 = combined_no2[combined_no2['combined_no2_value'].notnull()]

# Calculate mean and standard deviation
mean_value = combined_no2['combined_no2_value'].mean()
std_dev = combined_no2['combined_no2_value'].std()

# Calculate z-scores
combined_no2['z_score'] = (combined_no2['combined_no2_value'] - mean_value) / std_dev

# Identify hot and cold spots
hot_spots = combined_no2[combined_no2['z_score'] > 1.96]
cold_spots = combined_no2[combined_no2['z_score'] < -1.96]

hot_spots_result = hot_spots[['borough', 'z_score']]
cold_spots_result = cold_spots[['borough', 'z_score']]

hot_spots_result, cold_spots_result
```
